chunks: And from him, from Abī Jaʿfar, from Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim al-Bajalī, who said:
I saw Abā Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام praying in a shirt, having wrapped himself above it with a cloth while he was praying.
And from him, from ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, who said: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn wrote to al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ:
May a man perform the salat (prayer) while wearing an izār draped around himself over the shirt? So he wrote: “Yes.”

So there is no contradiction between these reports and what we mentioned earlier, because what is intended by the earlier reports is that a person should not wrap himself and cover himself in it as the Jews wrap themselves; and what we presented last is that he should drape himself with the izār so as to cover what has become exposed of him and conceal what has become uncovered of his body. And that which indicates what we have mentioned.

key_terms.اتَّزَرَ: wrapped himself with a waistcloth or covering cloth
key_terms.بِمِنْدِيلٍ: with a cloth used as an additional wrap
key_terms.يَسْتُرَ: to cover and conceal the body
key_terms.يَلْتَحِفَ: to wrap oneself up fully in a garment

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) wearing an izār wrapped over a shirt?
ai.summary: This report concerns the permissibility of performing salat (prayer) while wearing a shirt together with an additional wrapped cloth or izār. It clarifies that the prohibition in earlier reports refers to a specific manner of wrapping oneself, not to wearing an izār over a shirt for proper covering during prayer.
